frequency_question: What proportion of formal institutional accrediting agency revocation or termination processes initiated by the Department of Education are fully completed (reaching final determination) within an 85-day calendar window?
membership_rule: Includes any formal proceeding by the U.S. Department of Education to strip an agency of its recognized accrediting status. Excludes voluntary relinquishments or standard 5-year renewal reviews that do not involve revocation proceedings.

cases.name: ACICS recognition withdrawal proceedings (Obama/Trump transition era)

provenance_note: rate of 0% from only 2 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 2 major contested institutional accrediting revocation proceedings analyzed; both exceeded 200 days minimum due to mandatory statutory notice and comment periods.
known_gaps: Limited number of total federal accrediting agency death-penalty revocations, but procedural floors are legally mandated.
skeleton: Administrative process steps: (1) Staff initial review and recommendation (60 days minimum notice requirements); (2) Advisory committee meeting and public comment window (90-120 days statutory minimums); (3) Agency head review and final decision (60-90 days). Total sequential time minimum is roughly 210-270 days under standard Administrative Procedure Act and Higher Education Act constraints.
multiplier: 210 minimum required process days / 85 available calendar days
validity_reason: Statutory timelines under the Higher Education Act and administrative procedural requirements remain fixed unless Congress amends the underlying laws.
